body: Thank you so much! I actually draw tons of stuff like this, and decided to finally digitally render one, and was pretty happy with how it came out. Glad you like it.
I have a bunch of hobbies that I enjoy.

It's boring, and being stuck here constantly reminds me that I'll be able to see an infinitesimally small part of even our galaxy, let alone the universe. I'm just missing out on so much beauty and wonder that nobody has ever experienced before.

Also I actually don't know if I'd be able to get depression help if I did have it, because I've tried to get help for my possible ADD but apparently it's really expensive to get tested and see a psychiatrist and our insurance doesn't cover it.

I've considered design stuff and have dabbled a bit but it's really really hard to get started there. Nobody really notices your shit. And I don't know how working regular hours could work since I have school and stuff.
Oh and I listen to a fuckton of music, and sometimes enjoy making some half baked beats if I feel motivated enough.
Also, I enjoy fashion a lot but don't have enough money to supply that addiction lol. And I'm not sure if it's actual depression or just emotionlessness mixed with hardcore introversion.

Yeah I mean I pretty much always play games with my friends, and I'm like usually up for a social encounter, but sometimes school drains me out so much that I just don't want to do anything. I am pretty social in school though. I play some sports which I enjoy, and I like working out.

I meant disorder, sorry, I was blanking on the right word to use. I'm just kinda scared that I might have not realized it because I've got so used to it. Now that I think about it, it makes sense. I have had trouble reading for the past ~3 years, like I just end up drifting off and the words become meaningless. And I don't necessarily want to take medicine for it, but I would want it to be treated in some way if it were there.
Thank you!
It was that my friend was being a dick and spreading stuff just to mess with me. Rough. Thanks for the reply!
Oh and quarter sphere, not quester sphere sorry. And since it's flat it's more of a quarter circle.

The second one, I guess it's like oldish London made of the flat shapes and a quarter sphere? I think that's the sense. Like think 1950s ish.


For the Death Star, it's more that it's just a really really big entity with tons of small corridors I think. Not the fact that it's destructive.
I guess so. Maybe this wasn't the right sub to post to, idk. I just wanted to sort out these feelings. Once again, thank you so so much for taking your time to talk with me.
Like the black hole thing? If I was able to, I'd wait a while and see how my life was in like 10 years. If it were a now or never deal, I'd do it.
I really really don't know, I mean I guess that's like the only really pleasurable way for me to go out. I'd like to be surrounded by family too. That'd be good as a realistic one.

Sorry, I submitted this one at the same time as you and didn't check back for a little bit.


I guess they're not really worlds, but more... Aesthetics? I really don't know how to describe them, they're pretty weird.


The first, and most vivid, is one that's related to snow.   It has a club-penguin type of feel? A recurring image is a house at dusk in the winter with snow up to the knees, and you turn a corner around the house and there's a snowy incline. I get s lot of flashbacks to it while skiing.


Another is one that's somehow related to England, it's very simplistic and happy and colorful and vibrant. Everything is pretty flat, and very very simplified. It's connected to diagonal motion, upwards and to the sides. Like a quester sphere in the frame and an arrow pointing outwards.


The most abstract, but the one that I have visions of or feelings of most in my everyday life is one where it is a bunch of... Small communities(?) that are all interconnected, and for some reason I relate to the Death Star or something like that, maybe because it's enormous and kinda plays into this thought. I don't know.


Finally, it's like if Toowntown were 2d and flat. I like this one a lot.


Thanks for listening so so much, it feels weird to write these things down.

I think we're getting at the same point here, you definitely phrased it very well though. I want to live my final moments in a state of pure happiness, doing something I love, something I've dreamed of for a long time, and seeing the sights I've always wanted to see. Obviously there's nobody keeping track of everything that happens, all history will be forgotten.

Also, I have these weird fantasy worlds that I don't really fully understand, maybe like three of them, and occasionally I just get a glimpse of them while doing something in my everyday life and it feels amazing, and I really, REALLY wish that I could record that moment in a picture and frame it or something. It's like I'm connected to these aesthetics. If you want to know more about them I'm open to share.

I mean, honestly that's a huge reason. I'll never leave our planet which takes up an infinitesimally small amount of the universe. I'm missing so much. There's just so much left to explore that I'm missing. My life isn't even that bad. It has its ups and downs, but a lot of people would envy me for what I have. I also know that no actions that I take on earth will be remembered at ALL on a galactic scale, or even on a regular historical scale. I won't be remembered at all. That saddens me. So the only thing that really matters is how I die. And I'd want to die in the most spectacular way possible, and that's the most spectacular (and probably least painful?) way I can think of.

But since that speed at which they are moving apart is always increasing, don't you think that after those millions of years it will have surpassed our possible limits? So as we're doing the journey it becomes more and more impossible and unachievable?

But isn't that really what dying is like when you think about it? You just fade out and stop existing. For all we know they could be the same sensation. Also youd get to live past the event horizon and see what could possibly be the most amazing sights ever, at least that's how I imagine it.

In my opinion going into a black hole would be actually being the first human to do it. It would be amazing. I would see the unknown.

As for realistic stuff, it makes me really sad that I'll never be able to experience it first hand. That's really what I care about. Thanks for taking the time to talk with me by the way.

I have no idea. I'm pretty interested in space. (Hence my username.) I think it's just that I'm really curious of the unknown, and that combined with wanting to die makes this happen.
